study type: Cross-sectional analysis of a prospective study
exposure: Depression screening scores (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale)
outcome: Persistent bothersome urinary symptoms (at 12 months postpartum)
cohort: The study participants were 419 individuals from medically underserved communities with health disparities, enrolled in 'extending Maternal Care After Pregnancy,' a program providing 12 months of postpartum care.
finding: At 12 months postpartum, stress urinary incontinence was significantly associated with increasing body mass index at delivery and greater depression screening scores, while urgency urinary incontinence was significantly associated with increasing parity and higher anxiety screening scores.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was not associated with stress urinary incontinence.
